title: TF module: VPC observability stack (Prometheus + Grafana + OTel + log shipping)
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement a reusable Terraform module to provision an observability stack for Private (VPC) deployments. The module must support deploying Prometheus (kube-prometheus-stack), Grafana, an OpenTelemetry Collector, and a log-shipping agent (Vector/Fluentd) into customer-managed Kubernetes clusters via the Helm and Kubernetes providers. It should expose configuration knobs for cloud provider artifacts (S3/OpenSearch/managed services), persistent storage sizing, backups/remote-write, and network controls (private-only LB, internal ingress). Module must be idempotent, support zero-downtime minor upgrades, include health-checking automation (Terraform waiters + k8s probe validation), and provide smoke tests for acceptance. Acceptance criteria: terraform plan/apply completes without errors in a clean cluster; Prometheus is scraping targets and retaining metrics as configured; Grafana has base dashboards provisioned; OTel collector is receiving and forwarding traces/metrics; log agent ships logs to configured sink; documented upgrade and rollback runbooks exist.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Kickoff: scoped module boundaries. Decision: use Helm provider for releases to keep resource drift small and leverage upstream kube-prometheus-stack and grafana charts.

2026-03-01 - Design note: support two log-shipping sinks (S3 for long-term + OpenSearch/ELK for search). Provide examples for AWS and GCP but keep provider-agnostic interface (s3_bucket / object_store vs elastic_url).

2026-03-03 - Tradeoff: Bundled prometheus vs remote-write only. Chose bundled kube-prometheus-stack with optional remote_write to Thanos/remote storage to preserve compatibility for small customers and allow larger installs to offload storage.
2026-03-05 - Security review requested: module will create ServiceAccounts and RBAC rules; must support restricting secrets to KMS/HSM encryption. Filing security checklist (see files).

2026-03-07 - Implementation note: include terraform post-deploy validation using local-exec to run kubectl wait for deployments and curl readiness endpoints; run k8s Job to emit synthetic metric and trace to verify end-to-end.
2026-03-08 - Next: open PR skeleton with module interface + example usage for AWS EKS and on-prem k8s clusters. Add unit tests using terratest and nightly integration job in CI.
Related artifacts: design doc (confluence), terraform skeleton PR, example helm-values files in repo (links in files field).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (skeleton): create module inputs and outputs, helm/k8s provider pinning, simple example deploying kube-prometheus-stack and grafana with internal service
Phase 2 (features): add OTel collector deployment with pipelines configurable for traces/metrics/logs, add log shipping DaemonSet (Vector) and examples for S3/OpenSearch
Phase 3 (resilience): PVC sizing, PodDisruptionBudgets, pre-upgrade snapshot job for Prometheus TSDB, remote_write optionality, backup/restore guidance
Phase 4 (automation): terraform waiters/validation, terratest integration, CI pipeline to run the module against a disposable cluster
Phase 5 (docs + runbooks): upgrade/rollback runbooks, SLO health-check definitions, Grafana dashboard provisioning templates
upgrade_strategy: Minor upgrades: use helm upgrade with chart image tags; ensure PodDisruptionBudget and rollingUpdate strategy with maxUnavailable: 0 / maxSurge where supported
Data safety: run a pre-upgrade snapshot job for Prometheus TSDB (wal snapshot) before any TSDB-incompatible chart change; optional remote_write to Thanos/OpenTSDB to avoid data loss
Major upgrades: require a migration plan with an offline window for TSDB format changes; test migration path in staging with full restore from backup
Rollback: capture helm revisions and provide automated helm rollback steps in runbook; restore PVC from backup if rollback crosses incompatible storage formats
health_checks: Terraform-level: local-exec kubectl wait for deployments/daemonsets to be ready (timeout configurable)
Application-level: Prometheus /metrics endpoint reachable, target scrape count within expected range; Grafana /api/health returns OK; OTel collector /healthz and /metrics OK
Synthetic tests: a k8s Job that emits a test metric and span; verify metric appears in Prometheus and trace in collector export sink
Alerting: default alert rules for Prometheus: PrometheusDown, LowDiskSpace, HighTSDBRetentionPressure, CollectorCrashLooping; alerts route to ops via existing notification channels
notes_on_operators: Provide hints for sizing PVCs based on expected ingestion rate (tokens/sec -> samples/sec mapping), recommend retention tiers and cost tradeoffs
Recommend enabling remote_write to a long-term store for customers with >30d retention requirements
For on-prem/offline deployments, include an offline-mode for grafana provisioning (no external plugin downloads)
testing_plan: Unit: terraform fmt/lint and validate, helm chart value rendering
Integration: terratest to apply module in ephemeral k8s (kind/EKS/GKE) and run smoke tests (scraping, dashboard provisioning, log shipping)
E2E: run in staging Private VPC and run load test to validate scrape and log throughput and storage behavior
Chaos: simulate node termination and ensure no data-loss and successful reconvergence
open_questions: Which log sink should be the recommended default for Private customers (S3+OpenSearch combo vs managed ELK)?
Do we provide a hosted remote_write target as a Redwood managed service for customers who want cheaper operator experience?
What's the minimum supported Kubernetes version for the module? (proposal: >=1.26)
